report.source_text: On physical examination, his vitals were stable with blood pressure of 147/85 mmHg and heart rate of 98 beats per minute. He had swelling restricted to the dorsum of both hands with pitting edema (Fig. 1A). Examination of the joints showed tenderness suggestive of synovitis with restricted movements in bilateral proximal interphalangeal joint. Other clinical examinations including cardiovascular, respiratory, abdominal, and neurological examinations were unremarkable.

clinician.trajectory_summary: An 82-year-old Asian male presented with a 2-month history of symmetrical swelling over the dorsum of both hands, associated with pitting edema, joint tenderness, and restricted movement in the bilateral proximal interphalangeal joints. There were no systemic symptoms, history of malignancy, infection, or new medication exposures. Laboratory tests revealed elevated inflammatory markers (ESR 118 mm/hr, CRP 6.58 mg/dL), slight anemia, and hyperglycemia. Autoimmune serology (rheumatoid factor and anti-CCP antibodies) were not reported. Plain radiographs showed soft tissue swelling without joint space narrowing or bone erosion, excluding erosive arthritis. Physical examination confirmed synovitis-like tenderness and pitting edema localized to hands. No ultrasound data or treatment response data were available. These features support a diagnosis of bilateral RS3PE, characterized by symmetrical pitting edema and synovitis in elderly patients with elevated inflammatory markers and absence of typical rheumatoid arthritis features.
